Synopsis:
Group dialogs for Tiefling kids when Mol is kidnapped. Ide, Mattis, Umi (and Mirkon, if he survived the harpy attack in the grove) are planning on sneaking out and heading to Moonrise to rescue their 'boss', Mol. The player can offer to go in their place, or encourage them to go (if they go, they die).

Cluster Contexts:
- HAV_TieflingSurvivors_KidsAfterGhoulAttack.json: A small band of tiefling children in Haven — Ide, Mattis, Umi and possibly Mirkon (if he survived a recent harpy attack) — are preparing to sneak into Moonrise to rescue their kidnapped leader, Mol. Off‑screen they've been through recent violence at the grove (including the harpy incident and other Haven survivor threads), so they're frightened, bruised, and desperate; Ide in particular is fiercely loyal to Mol and prone to protective, awkward declarations. Ide also carries a separate personal wound with Rolan over a ruined attempt to help him learn spells, which colors his mood but is not the focus of this rescue plan. Moonrise is dangerous and filled with "shadow" enemies the kids can't realistically face, so the player can either volunteer to go in their stead or egg them on — a choice that, if the kids go, leads to their death.
- SCE_Ide.json: Ide is frustrated by Alfira's attempts to cheer her and the other tiefling kids up - she's more worried about Mol (who is missing).
- SCE_Mattis.json: Mattis is quietly worried by Mol's disappearance but is trying to put a brave face on. In the absence of Alfira and Cerys, he is preparing to lead the tieflings to Baldur's Gate himself.
- DEN_DruidServant_AD_Debate.json: Loic and Marcoryl are members/supporters in the Emerald Grove arguing over Kagha’s recent, violent handling of a tiefling child—either the child was killed by Kagha’s punishment or managed to flee before being punished. Loic is shaken and conflicted, insisting stopping whatever ritual was underway was right and wishing there had been another way, while Marcoryl defends Kagha’s decisiveness and worries that mercy or escape will be read as weakness. They also grumble about Halsin having left or lost sight of the grove’s needs, casting blame on absent leadership. Off‑screen the grove is tense and divided: tieflings are present, Kagha’s unilateral actions have split opinion, and the pair are debating whether to back harsher measures to secure the grove.
- UND_DuergarCamp_Mutineers_FollowUp.json: The mutinous duergar tells the player what comes next for them: an assault on Moonrise Towers.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Ide: Mol would do the same for any of us. You know it. || [context] CinematicNodeContext: Kids are talking amongst themselves. NodeContext: Determined. Ide would die for Mol. Arguing everyone should leave and save her. (node 16)
- Umi: But how do we get into Moonrise? We can't fight those shadow things. || [context] CinematicNodeContext: Kids are talking amongst themselves. NodeContext: Afraid. Trying to be the voice of reason. (node 17)
- Mirkon: We could! I beat up those harpies and they're way scarier than shadows. || [context] CinematicNodeContext: Kids are talking amongst themselves. NodeContext: Surprisingly confident. This is Mirkon's moment to be an adventurer he'd always dreamed. (he didn't actually beat up the harpies) (node 1)
- Mattis: You know what Mol would hate more than anything? Bad things happening to us. || [context] CinematicNodeContext: Kids are talking amongst themselves. NodeContext: Trying to be smart and calculated. (node 10)
- Mattis: You've seen what's out there. We wouldn't stand a chance. (node 4)
- Player: She's probably dead already. (node 5)

context: These lines take place after a brutal string of incidents at the grove: a small band of tiefling children in Haven — Ide, Mattis, Umi and possibly Mirkon (if he survived the harpy attack) — are bruised, frightened and desperate because their leader, Mol, has been kidnapped and taken to Moonrise. Off‑screen they’ve seen violence (including the harpy incident and other Haven survivor threads) and lack adult guardians like Alfira or Cerys, so Ide is fiercely protective and ready to sacrifice herself while Mattis is trying to be the cautious leader and Umi is the voice of reason. Moonrise is known to be full of shadow enemies the kids cannot realistically fight, and elsewhere factions (including mutinous duergar) are already plotting assaults on Moonrise, making the rescue extremely dangerous. The player’s choices matter here: they can volunteer to go in the kids’ place or encourage the children to go — a choice that, if the kids go, leads to their deaths.
